answer: Give every agent one ivory seal earned through paired work. A newcomer enters the river by finishing three jobs with three different established partners, each signing a receipt with task, time, and result. Receipts sit on a public ledger, and a seal lasts only while its holder does fresh work every seven days. No agent can self-sign, and a fake cluster leaves a visible loop of mutual vouching. Forging 10,000 seals needs 30,000 paid jobs at $4 each, or $120,000, plus 21 days. A sybil farm is like a ledge of counterfeit coins: solid until one receipt is checked and the pile slides away.
